comments.author: Cat Riona
comments.text:
So a few things re: barbells... 

1.⁠ ⁠Firstly, think about why these exercises have been recommended. Free weights automatically involve much more balance and core strength - which is super useful to us as runners! So ultimately, what you want to do is build up to being confident to use the free weights. HOWEVER… This doesn’t necessarily mean go straight in with a barbell! Can you use two light dumbbells instead and work your way up? 

2.⁠ ⁠⁠Think also about confidence. While it is nice to remain in our comfort zones… we are not going to see the same improvements if we stay there! So… can you do ONE set with a barbell, before moving back to your favoured machines? What I find it really good to do in a gym where I don’t know how it all works and I’m feeling a little shy (and I go to a lot of new gyms with travelling!) is if I can warm up on a bike or treadmill where I have a good view of the gym, I can observe how everyone moves and works, and then gain some confidence that way. Also, don’t be afraid to ask a gym PT!

3. Of course, machines are better than nothing. Use it while you get used to the new environment of course, but try not to become reliant on static machines (all gyms tend to have weights, sometimes machines change!)

workouts.name: Pre-Run Activation: Quads & Hamstrings (for suffering knees!)
workouts.description:
See videos below for full exercise demonstrations (warning, may contain mobilising moggies!) 

An Activation workout is done before a run or a harder strength session to 'wake up' muscles which may not want to move fluidly straight from the off! 

Running involves the majority of muscles in the body, so we want everything to be firing well. However, this does also mean that sometimes we compensate and use smaller muscles to do the work of larger ones if we're not fully mobilised. In starting to increase bloodflow and warm the core temperature of our main drivers to running, we can often move better as a result of targeted activation. 

To activate and mobilise hips, quads and hamstrings, complete: 

1-2 sets of 8 (each side if applicable): 

1. Hip Kickbacks
2. Banded Crab Walks
3. Banded Knee Drives 
4. Dynamic Hamstring Stretch

workouts.name: Pre-Run Activation: Quads & Hamstrings (for suffering knees!)
workouts.description:
See videos below for full exercise demonstrations (warning, may contain mobilising moggies!) 

An Activation workout is done before a run or a harder strength session to 'wake up' muscles which may not want to move fluidly straight from the off! 

Running involves the majority of muscles in the body, so we want everything to be firing well. However, this does also mean that sometimes we compensate and use smaller muscles to do the work of larger ones if we're not fully mobilised. In starting to increase bloodflow and warm the core temperature of our main drivers to running, we can often move better as a result of targeted activation. 

To activate and mobilise hips, quads and hamstrings, complete: 

1-2 sets of 8 (each side if applicable): 

1. Hip Kickbacks
2. Banded Crab Walks
3. Banded Knee Drives 
4. Dynamic Hamstring Stretch

workouts.description:
See videos below for full exercise demonstrations. Perform slow and controlled - these should feel like difficult stretches which challenge your range of motion and instill great quality movement patterns, NOT 'sheer' strength work. Warning: videos may contain 'helpful' felines...

If done after a run, no need to warm up. If done as a stand-alone session, ease into full range of motion - try to lean slightly more into the stretch each exhale, as your body relaxes.

2 x 45s (each side if applicable): 
1. Single Leg Hip Circle
2. Standing Quad stretch
3. Standing Hamstring Stretch into calf stretch
4. Sitting Banded Calf Stretch
5. Toe walk

workouts.name: Pre-Run Activation: Quads & Hamstrings (for suffering knees!)
workouts.description:
See videos below for full exercise demonstrations (warning, may contain mobilising moggies!) 

An Activation workout is done before a run or a harder strength session to 'wake up' muscles which may not want to move fluidly straight from the off! 

Running involves the majority of muscles in the body, so we want everything to be firing well. However, this does also mean that sometimes we compensate and use smaller muscles to do the work of larger ones if we're not fully mobilised. In starting to increase bloodflow and warm the core temperature of our main drivers to running, we can often move better as a result of targeted activation. 

To activate and mobilise hips, quads and hamstrings, complete: 

1-2 sets of 8 (each side if applicable): 

1. Hip Kickbacks
2. Banded Crab Walks
3. Banded Knee Drives 
4. Dynamic Hamstring Stretch
